items.question: From whom must this teaching be carefully concealed in the mortal world?
premises: The teaching must be concealed
Concealment requires deliberate effort
The lowest people are excluded
items.inference: This knowledge must be zealously hidden from unworthy people in the mortal world.
items.plain_english: It must be carefully concealed in the mortal world from the lowest of men.

items.question: To what kind of recipient may this teaching rightly be given?
premises: The teaching may be given
The recipient should be previously accomplished
The recipient must be tested for one year
items.inference: Transmission is permitted only to a proven and tested adept.
items.plain_english: It should be given to one who is already accomplished and has been tested for one year.

items.question: Which chapter concludes the teaching that emerged from Candradvīpa?
premises: The text emerged from Candradvīpa
A chapter is being identified
It is the fifth chapter
items.inference: This marks the conclusion of the fifth chapter of the Candradvīpa teaching.
items.plain_english: Thus ends the fifth chapter that emerged from Candradvīpa.

items.question: Through whose grace has the determination of the Kaula teaching been understood?
premises: The speaker claims knowledge
The knowledge concerns Kaula determination
Grace of the Kaula lord enabled it
items.inference: Understanding of the Kaula doctrine arises through the lord's grace.
items.plain_english: O Lord of the Kaulas, by your grace I have understood the determination of the Kaula teaching.

items.question: What is the declared identity and essential nature of the individual soul?
premises: The soul has been declared
Its identity is questioned
Its essential nature is questioned
items.inference: The teaching must clarify both who the soul is and what its nature is.
items.plain_english: Who is that soul that has been declared, and what is the nature of the soul?

items.question: Into what reality does the individual soul ultimately dissolve?
premises: The soul undergoes dissolution
The locus of dissolution is unknown
A complete explanation is requested
items.inference: The teaching must reveal the final locus of the soul's dissolution.
items.plain_english: And into what does it dissolve? Tell me all of that.

items.question: What supreme qualities define the ultimate reality identified as the soul?
premises: The soul is identified as supreme
It is partless and eternal
It is free from disease and stain
items.inference: The true soul is the supreme, undivided, eternal, and pure reality.
items.plain_english: He is supreme, partless, eternal, free from disease and stainless.

items.question: How is the supreme individual soul identified in terms of haṃsa and power?
premises: The soul is described as supreme
That soul is identified as haṃsa
It is characterized as power and individual
items.inference: The supreme soul is the haṃsa, the individual endowed with power.
uncertainties: The precise sense of śakti+pudgalaḥ is context-dependent.
items.plain_english: That soul who is supreme is indeed the haṃsa, the individual of power.

items.question: Where is the life-breath that fills with air situated within living beings?
premises: There is air that fills as breath
This breath is situated somewhere
It is present in all beings
items.inference: The vital breath pervades and abides in all living beings.
items.plain_english: The air that fills as breath is situated in all living beings.

items.question: What is the soul called immediately upon leaving the physical body?
premises: The soul leaves the body
A new designation applies at that moment
It is called supreme Śiva
items.inference: Upon leaving the body, the soul is recognized as supreme Śiva.
items.plain_english: As soon as he leaves the body, he is called the supreme Śiva.

items.question: How is this secret teaching transmitted and inwardly perceived by the practitioner?
premises: Something is heard in the ear
It comes through traditional succession
The goddess is addressed as witness
items.inference: The teaching is received inwardly through an unbroken lineage.
items.plain_english: O Goddess, it is heard in the ear, having come down through the succession of tradition.

items.question: What transformative power does merely hearing this knowledge possess for the seeker?
premises: The knowledge is merely heard
Hearing itself is an instrument
The fair-faced one is addressed
items.inference: Even the mere hearing of this knowledge has spiritual efficacy.
items.plain_english: O fair-faced one, by this mere knowledge that has been heard...

items.question: What disciplined practice over six months leads to a state free from bondage?
premises: Practice continues for six months
The practitioner cultivates a renunciant state
That state is free from bondage
items.inference: Six months of dedicated practice yields freedom from bondage.
uncertainties: kāṣāyaṃ may refer to an ochre-robed or ascetic state.
items.plain_english: Whoever practices for six months in that ochre state, free from bondage...

items.question: What benefits result from sustained practice of this soul-knowledge?
premises: The practitioner becomes free from all diseases
The practitioner gains union with yogis
These are results of practice
items.inference: The practice brings healing and communion with accomplished yogis.
items.plain_english: ...becomes freed from all diseases and attains union with the yogis.

items.question: What teaching has now been fully communicated to Bhairavī regarding the soul?
premises: A teaching has been told
It concerns the practice of the soul
Bhairavī is the recipient
items.inference: The instruction on the soul's practice has been completely conveyed.
items.plain_english: O Bhairavī, this practice concerning the soul has been told to you.

items.question: To which resolved and fully prepared disciple should this teaching be given?
premises: The teaching may be given
The recipient must be endowed with all states
The recipient must have firm resolve
items.inference: Only a fully prepared and resolute disciple is fit to receive it.
items.plain_english: It should be given to one who is endowed with all states and has a resolved mind.

items.question: Under what circumstances must the essential Kaula teaching be withheld?
premises: The Kaula essence is highly sacred
It originates in the yoginīs
It must not be given indiscriminately
items.inference: The essential Kaula teaching, born of the yoginīs, must not be given to the unfit.
uncertainties: The syntactic relation of sambhavam to the rest of the clause is slightly ambiguous.
items.plain_english: The essential Kaula teaching, which has its origin in the yoginīs, must not be given.

items.question: What transformation of the body follows the removal of ignorance's veil?
premises: The body was struck by ignorance's veil
A change has occurred now
The body is now pure
items.inference: Through this teaching, the body once veiled by ignorance becomes pure.
items.plain_english: Today my body, once struck by the veil of ignorance, is pure.

items.question: What auspicious knowledge is sought to overcome the deception of time?
premises: The seeker wishes to hear further
The topic is time's deception
The sought teaching is auspicious
items.inference: The next instruction concerns the auspicious means of overcoming time and death.
items.plain_english: Now I wish to hear the auspicious teaching on overcoming the deception of time.

items.question: Can death truly be destroyed through the teaching about to be revealed?
premises: The teacher promises instruction
There is no doubt in the claim
Death can be destroyed
items.inference: The teaching confidently asserts a method for destroying death.
items.plain_english: I shall tell you, without doubt, how death is destroyed.

items.question: What subtle nectar practice affects even the wise practitioner internally?
premises: There is a tip of nectar
It involves the essence of juice
Even the wise are affected by it
items.inference: A subtle internal nectar process acts powerfully, even on the wise.
uncertainties: The exact physiological referent of amṛta+agraṃ is esoteric.
items.plain_english: Even the wise one is burned at the tip of nectar by the essence of the juice.

items.question: How should the practitioner draw in the vital air to conquer time?
premises: The practice involves the root of tongue and palate
The practitioner acts on the air
The air should be drawn in slowly
items.inference: The method requires slowly drawing in the breath at the root of the tongue and palate.
items.plain_english: Placing it at the root of the tongue and palate, one should slowly drink in the air.

items.question: What duration of this breath practice is required to destroy aging and death?
premises: The practice is performed for one year
The practice must be sustained
Old age and death are destroyed
items.inference: One year of sustained practice destroys old age and death.
items.plain_english: When practiced for one year, old age and death are destroyed.

items.question: What immunity to poison results from mastery of this yogic practice?
premises: The practitioner may be bitten by great serpents
Poison normally enters the body
In this case poison does not enter
items.inference: Mastery of the practice grants immunity even to deadly serpent venom.
items.plain_english: Poison does not enter the body, even if one is bitten by great serpents.
